title: Curly Hamner's royalty check and Cobb's unpaid tune
summary: Cobb complains that Curly Hamner, Gladys and Hampton each got $2,200 on a tune Milton Buckner wrote and that he never received royalties on his own copyrighted tune.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: And I think I feel free today to say things that happened that I didn't think was right and -- in the music business. I'm in it, and I wouldn't want it done to me. But Curly Hamner came in the band, and Curly got a check for
$2,200.00 and Gladys got one for $2,200.00. Hamp got one for $2,200.00, and Milton Buckner did the tune, and he got 600.00.
Well, why did Curly get (inaudible)?
You're asking me questions, Stanley, I can't answer. I want to know why too. And he come in (inaudible) big long check from the record company. Or publishing company, I should have said.
Well, now, Curly, did he play drums (inaudible)?
Yes.
But he wasn't really a drummer, was he? I mean wasn't he --
Dancer.
Yes.

But he come in and got very influential. He's one of the reasons I left the band because people got gigs (inaudible) over that and disrespect-wise and everything. And I wasn't going to have mine around it. So I knew when to put my notice in, and I'll let you know about that too.
Well, Curly presumably has gotten his name on some of these numbers.
Huh?
Curly had gotten his name --
Came right (inaudible) he wouldn't know a note if he saw one, but he got paid for something he didn't --

and, see, this is -- I don't think it's right. And I'm not there now, and I could afford to say it, and you can blast it if you want to. That's taking money for -- Arnett Cobb's (inaudible) money for and Swing and never received a quarter. That's Hamp and company.
Don't you have your name on it?
I got copyright on it.
Well, how come they didn't give you the money?
You asking me? Go ask him. Ga-ga-ga-g-g-- he's always got some excuse. That's how come he's a millionaire and I'm not.
Yeah, but --
I get bitter about these things today.
(Inaudible).
Because you're taking something from somebody that doesn't belong to you.
Yeah, but you really (inaudible) talking about it (inaudible) that's very funny because that must be the record company.
